findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - A teammate creates and drops the empty upgrade fix after this checkout's last fetch.
`repo.default_config` fetches only the default branch (src/forge/repo.py:713), so the new fix record is unavailable locally. `ls-remote` finds the branch, but the suggested `git branch -d fix/<name>` fails because no local branch exists and cannot remove the remote branch. The upgrade remains blocked. The named test creates and drops the fix in the same checkout, so it misses this case.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - After this checkout sees an empty dropped fix, a teammate restores it, commits other work, and drops it again.
This check examines the stale remote-tracking branch before `task.fix_drop` fetches and restores the current branch (src/forge/task.py:817). Upgrade then changes the fix's goal without checking the newly fetched commits, so the teammate's work enters the upgrade branch instead of causing the promised refusal. The new test performs the drop and upgrade in one checkout and does not cover this.
findings.title: Recheck the fix after restoring its latest remote commits

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A user restores the fix, edits a file in its worktree, and runs upgrade from the default branch before committing.
The dirty-work check refuses but names `forge close <name>`. Close reviews committed `HEAD` (src/forge/close.py:295); if the edit is the only product work, it refuses because the fix contains only records (src/forge/task.py:728). If other work was already committed, close can publish without the uncommitted edit. The named command therefore does not finish the work that caused the refusal.
findings.title: Give an actionable next step for uncommitted fix work

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A fix with the upgrade's name has been started for a different purpose, but its owner has not committed product changes yet.
A different `why` alone enters the reuse path even when the fix has never been dropped or restored. With a clean worktree, line 146 replaces its Why and Done-when and continues the upgrade in its branch, silently taking over the active fix. The previous code refused this collision. The existing collision test uses an uncommitted record without a branch field, so it does not exercise this valid started-fix state.
findings.title: Preserve active fixes that were never dropped
